overview.problemStatement: Registration ends at the screen: no confirmation to keep, no reminder the day before, no follow-up afterwards, and organisers cannot tell whether anyone was emailed.
overview.proposedSolution: Four lifecycle templates sent through the existing Mailtrap transport: confirmation at registration, a 24-hour reminder, and a post-event thank-you with a feedback link. Idempotency keys prevent duplicates, failures are logged and retried within a bounded budget, and an opt-out suppresses optional email while confirmation still sends.
overview.targetAudience: Attendees who register for events and organisers who need to know delivery happened.
assumptions: The Mailtrap transport and emailEvents log already exist and stay in place.
Cron infrastructure in convex/crons.ts can host the reminder and follow-up sweeps.
Templates live in code for this version.

userStories.title: Know my registration is real
userStories.want: a confirmation email with the event details and my ticket
userStories.benefit: I have a record outside the app

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a successful registration, a confirmation email is sent to the attendee address within 60 seconds containing the event title, date, location, and a link to the ticket.

userStories.title: Be reminded before the event
userStories.want: a reminder about a day before
userStories.benefit: I do not forget the event I registered for

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a confirmed registration for an event starting in roughly 24 hours, exactly one reminder is sent to attendees who have not opted out.
Given an event that has ended, a thank-you email with a feedback link is sent to confirmed attendees who have not opted out.

userStories.title: Trust that email is not duplicated or silently lost
userStories.benefit: I am not spammed and I do not miss one because a job re-ran

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the reminder job runs repeatedly, or a retry occurs, no registration receives the same lifecycle email twice.
Given a provider failure, the failure is recorded with its reason, retried within a bounded budget, and visible in the admin delivery log; the registration itself never fails because email did.

userStories.title: Control what I receive
userStories.want: to opt out of reminders and follow-ups
userStories.benefit: my inbox stays mine while I still receive the confirmation I need

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an attendee who opts out of lifecycle email, reminders and thank-yous stop, and the registration confirmation is still delivered.

userStories.title: See what was sent
userStories.benefit: I can answer whether they got the email without guessing

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a registration, the admin can see which lifecycle emails were sent, failed, or skipped, with timestamps.
Given any lifecycle email, the rendered content contains only that recipient data, and no message is addressed to more than one attendee.

functionalRequirements.text: A lifecycle template registry MUST define four templates - registration_confirmation, reminder_24h, post_event_thankyou, feedback_request - each with subject, HTML, and text bodies.
Registration MUST schedule the confirmation asynchronously so the mutation returns without waiting on the provider.
A scheduled job MUST select confirmed registrations whose event starts within the reminder window of 24 plus or minus 1 hours and enqueue reminders.
A scheduled job MUST select registrations whose event ended within the follow-up window and enqueue the thank-you.
Each send MUST carry an idempotency key of registrationId plus template, recorded before dispatch, so a repeat run sends nothing.
A failed send MUST be recorded with the provider reason, retried with a bounded budget, and never throw into the registration path.
An attendee MUST be able to set an email preference that suppresses reminder and thank-you sends while leaving confirmation in place.
The admin MUST be able to read per-registration delivery rows for the lifecycle templates.
Templates MUST render through one escaping renderer; no recipient data may appear in another recipient message.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Confirmation is transactional and MUST NOT be suppressed by the lifecycle preference; reminders and thank-yous are optional and MUST honour it.
Registration latency MUST NOT depend on the email provider; the mutation completes before the send is attempted.
Every lifecycle email MUST be sent to exactly one recipient; no BCC fan-out, and no other attendee data in the body.
Retries MUST be bounded and observable; a permanently failing registration MUST stop retrying and remain visible as failed rather than looping.
